problems.statement: A self-reinforcing burnout loop: vacancies drive agency use; agency nurses cannot charge or precept and need buddy orientation, so permanent RNs absorb charge and orientation load; overload drives resignations (about two quarters later), which raises vacancies and agency use again.

Larchmere's RN pay has fallen behind the regional market (101% to 91% of median), which raises resignations and agency rates. It is a real contributing and entry-level factor, but not the main driver of volume.

Presented explanation: this is an external market problem, with St. Brennan's poaching Larchmere's nurses. The timing and scale do not fit, because the vacancy rise and resignation climb began in 2024, before St. Brennan's opened in March 2026, and only 19 of 98 known leavers went there.
Agency cost growth is mostly a volume effect (about 77%), with a smaller rate effect (about 23%) from the contract wage-index escalator and above-market Vantage rates.

The 4 West orientation-coordinator pilot failed (the CNO's reading). It actually reduced workload, exhaustion and resignations versus matched units. The CNO judged it at Q1 2026, when resignations were still driven by leavers who had decided before or soon after the pilot started.

A $15,000 sign-on bonus funded by suspending the charge and preceptor differentials will worsen the loop. It adds hires who need preceptors while cutting recognition for the people who precept, and the 2025 bonus trial raised hires but not net vacancy.
Recruitment speed or the hiring pipeline is a main cause of the vacancy problem.
Agency staffing causes patient harm (falls with injury).

causalClaims.from: High vacancy and agency share on a unit
causalClaims.to: Charge and buddy-orientation burden on permanent RNs

causalClaims.from: Workload relief on 4 West (educator plus charge cap)
Pay falling behind the regional median

actions.action: Extend the 4 West model (educator-led agency orientation and a cap on charge shifts, backfilled by float RNs) first to the 7 highest-agency units, and track resignations and exhaustion.
actions.rationale: It is the only intervention with matched-unit evidence of breaking the overload-to-resignation loop.

actions.action: Do not suspend the charge and preceptor differentials. Keep them, or raise them.
actions.rationale: Suspending them removes recognition from the staff who carry the load, and charge-qualified nurses have said they would leave or give up the qualification.

actions.action: Reject the $15,000 sign-on bonus as designed, with its funding source.
actions.rationale: New hires add preceptor load, the 2025 bonus trial raised hiring but not net vacancy and saw 16 post-clawback departures, and the funding cuts retention pay.

actions.action: Renegotiate or rebid the Vantage agency contract (escalator clause, 6-8% lower competing quotes) before the 2027-01-01 renewal.
actions.rationale: The rate effect is real, about 23% of the increase, and a cheaper contract is available at low risk.

actions.action: Adjust the RN pay scale toward the regional median for the experienced 2-8 year band, with retention-focused pay.
actions.rationale: Pay is 91% of median and is cited by 17% of leavers, so it is a secondary but real factor. Target it at retention, not at new hires.

actions.action: Pause the plan to out-hire St. Brennan's, and keep the recruitment campaign modest.
actions.rationale: St. Brennan's accounts for a minority of leavers, and hiring into an overloaded unit adds to preceptor burden.

actions.action: Restructure NUR-114: allow vetted agency RNs to take on some orientation or charge duties, and use longer agency assignments to cut repeated orientation.
actions.rationale: The 13-week rotation of travelers forces constant buddy orientation, so this could cut the burden, but it has not been tested.

actions.action: Run a unit-month falls analysis adjusted for acuity and age before drawing conclusions about agency and safety.
actions.rationale: The current falls data is confounded by acuity and age.

nextEvidence: Cost and resignation results from extending the 4 West model to more units, including cost per avoided resignation against agency spend.
Retention and attrition of the 2-8 year RN cohort by pay band, plus what leavers and stayers say they would accept for charge and preceptor pay.
Unit-month falls analysis adjusted for acuity, census and age, with the assigned nurse recorded.
output.summary: Agency spend tripled mainly through volume (77%), not market rates. The cause is an internal loop: vacancies bring in agency staff, who cannot charge or precept, so permanent RNs carry charge and orientation load, burn out and resign about two quarters later, which adds vacancies. St. Brennan's opened after the trend began and took only 19 of 98 known leavers. The 4 West pilot worked against matched units; the CNO judged it too early. The bonus, funded by cutting charge and preceptor differentials, would worsen the loop. Fund workload relief, keep the differentials, and rebid the agency contract.
